components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        title:
          title: Title
          description: >-
            Optional honorific title of the pet owner (MR, MRS, MS or DR). When present it is
            combined with the last name to form the 'salutation'.
          type: string
          maxLength: 10
          example: DR
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: >-
            The postal address of the pet owner. Accepted on input for backward compatibility;
            when structured address fields are supplied they take precedence. On output this is the
            composed address: the normalized addressLine1, with a single space and the normalized
            addressLine2 appended when addressLine2 is present.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        addressLine1:
          title: Address line 1
          description: >-
            The first line of the structured postal address. Preferred over the flat 'address' when
            present. Normalized like 'address' (trim/collapse whitespace, upper-case, expand
            ST/RD/AVE) and stored and returned when supplied.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        addressLine2:
          title: Address line 2
          description: >-
            The optional second line of the structured postal address (e.g. unit or level).
            Normalized like addressLine1 and appended to the composed 'address' when present.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'Unit 4'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        postcode:
          title: Postcode
          description: >-
            Optional 4-digit postcode. When present it must be valid for the owner's city per the
            fixed region table (NSW 2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099); a city with no known
            region accepts any 4-digit postcode. Stored and returned when supplied.
          type: string
          pattern: '^[0-9]{4}$'
          example: '2000'
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^[0-9]*$'
          example: '6085551023'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: The email address of the pet owner. Stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: The date the pet owner was registered. Defaults to the server's current date when omitted.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        birthDate:
          title: Birth date

# Idempotent create: when the request carries an 'Idempotency-Key' already recorded for a completed
# create, respond 200 with the originally created owner and skip the whole create pipeline (so no
# duplicate is made and no later quota/duplicate rule fires). Otherwise take the 'proceed' branch to
# run the normal pipeline; the key is recorded against the new owner by the 'register' step below.

  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckIdempotencyKey
  govern: [ transaction ]
  outputs:
    proceed: validate

# Validate required fields first, so a missing/blank field is a 400 listing every
# offending field before the body is mapped to an entity.
validate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidateOwnerFields
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: validatePostcode

# city's region. Absent postcode is accepted (optional). Runs after the required-field validation,
# so the city is known before its region range is applied.
validatePostcode:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidatePostcode
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: checkCityCapacity

checkCityCapacity:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckOwnerCityCapacity
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: checkDailyCreateLimit

checkDailyCreateLimit:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckOwnerDailyCreateLimit
  govern: [ transaction ]

  govern: [ transaction ]

# so owners with the same last name and postcode share it automatically. Still used for the
# household member count and level ceiling; duplicate detection no longer keys off it.

# (64-hex SHA-256 over normalizedTelephone|lowerEmail|soundex(lastName)) equals an existing owner's,
# ignoring soft-deleted owners. This is the single duplicate rule: the former separate
# household-duplicate 409 block no longer applies. Runs before save so the not-yet-saved owner is
# not compared against itself.
checkIdentity:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckOwnerIdentityUnique
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignHouseholdMemberCount

# not-yet-saved owner. Runs after the shared householdId has been assigned and back-filled.
assignHouseholdMemberCount:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignHouseholdMemberCount
  govern: [ transaction ]

## Summary

I implemented the `capacityWarning` field for created owners, mirroring the existing `bulkSignupWarning` pattern. The warning is `true` when the owner's city already holds **40–49** owners (approaching the capacity limit of 50); the hard 409 rejection at 50 (`CheckOwnerCityCapacity`) is untouched.

Changes:

1. **`AssignCapacityWarning.java`** (new function class) — counts existing owners in the city case-insensitively over `findAll()` (same matching as the capacity check), running before save so the new owner is excluded, and sets `capacityWarning = 40 ≤ inCity ≤ 49`.

2. **`owners.POST.yml`** — wired the new `assignCapacityWarning` step into the pipeline (after `assignBulkSignupWarning`, before `assignPossibleDuplicate`), governed by the same transaction.

3. **`Owner.java`** — added the `capacityWarning` `Boolean` field (`@Column(name = "capacity_warning")`) with getter/setter.

4. **`openapi.yml`** — added a read-only `capacityWarning` boolean under the Owner schema, so the generated `OwnerDto` gets the field and MapStruct auto-maps the same-named property (no explicit mapper change needed).

5. **Schema files** (hsqldb, h2, postgres, mysql) — added the `capacity_warning` column so persistence/read-back works across all DBs.

The `Cp54Tests` warning test and the `Cp18Tests` hard-limit test both pass, along with the rest of the suite.
